clue.text: Murmur softly and coppers shut up

parts.note: to coo is to murmur softly, like a dove
coppers are pennies, abbreviated p

explanation.surface: Someone whispers while the police lock a suspect away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but here it means copper coins, pennies, abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: To coop up an animal or person is to confine them in a small pen.

clue.text: Uppity class getting into a knot

indicators.note: in a down clue, uppity says the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: rank means class or social standing

explanation.surface: Snobbish people find themselves tied up in a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uppity' turns RANK upwards to give KNAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A knar is a knot or gnarled lump in the wood of a tree.

clue.text: Light or heavy length of wood?

explanation.surface: A question about whether a piece of timber is light or heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of light is a beam, and so is a thick timber supporting a roof.

clue.text: Butt in here

parts.note: reads like an invitation to interrupt, but butt is a cigarette end and here is where it is stubbed out

explanation.surface: An invitation to interrupt a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish for stubbing out cigarette ends is where a butt goes.

clue.text: There's little publicity on official run

parts.note: an ad is a short advertisement, a little publicity
a minister is a government official

explanation.surface: A politician's campaign gets only a little press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts AD above MINISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer a business or country is to manage or run it.

clue.text: Ladies who number letters?

parts.note: to count is to number things
esses are the letters S, spelt out

explanation.surface: A riddle about women who keep tally of their correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a noun, but it is the verb, to COUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Countesses are noblewomen, wives of earls or counts, so they are titled ladies.

clue.text: Dwelling on street with difficult ingress

indicators.note: difficult says the letters of ingress are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A house on a road whose entrance is hard to get into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult' rearranges the letters of the entrance word. 'Dwelling' looks like a home, but it is the verb, as in dwelling on a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressing a point means emphasising it, giving it lingering attention.

clue.text: The guy appearing with day's end

parts.note: and means with, joining things together

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A man who turns up at nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy is a common man's name, a familiar way of naming some fellow.

clue.text: A point about Naval ratings' decoration

indicators.note: about says the word for point surrounds the sailors

parts.note: a dot is a point
RN is the Royal Navy
ratings are ordinary sailors, men

explanation.surface: A medal given to ordinary sailors in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the point around the navy and its sailors. Ratings are sailors below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: An adornment is an ornament or embellishment added for beauty.

clue.text: A limitation when father set about breaking mare

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the word for father encloses the rearranged horse

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for father

indicators.note: breaking says the letters of mare are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A father puts limits on training a wild horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' a horse is training it, so the surface reads naturally; here it is the anagram signal, and 'set about' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A parameter is a set boundary or limit within which something must operate.

clue.text: A turn in times past

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in it's your go

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having a go at something long before.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means before now, back in an earlier period.

clue.text: Don't include the circle with German following

indicators.note: following puts the German word after the circle

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave a group of friends out when a German joins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With German' asks for the German for 'with', MIT, which comes after O.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, the imperative of excluding.

clue.text: Some people fear having to use a hearing aid

indicators.note: some says only part of the words people fear is taken

explanation.surface: Many dread the day they need a hearing aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes the last three letters of 'people fear'. The definition is playful: the organ itself is what aids hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing is literally what helps a person hear, a witty view of a hearing aid.

clue.text: Men agitated about business proceed to ring around

indicators.note: about puts the reworked men around the abbreviation for business
agitated says the letters of men are stirred into a new order

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
to pass is to proceed or go on

explanation.surface: Excited men round off business by going for a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring around' looks like phoning round, but it means to surround.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass something is to surround or enclose it, as a ring does.

clue.text: Some lowly creatures possibly warm others

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Humble animals might give warmth to other beings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges WARM OTHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: These soil-dwelling invertebrates are a byword for lowliness.

clue.text: A woman's not in favour of standing

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
stance is a way of standing, or a position taken

explanation.surface: A woman opposes the stand being taken.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of the definition stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a female first name.

clue.text: Crazy character-had trouble in consequence

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters inside the word for consequence

parts.note: matter means consequence or importance, as in it is of no matter

indicators.note: trouble says the letters of had are disturbed and reordered

explanation.surface: A lunatic got into difficulty as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joining 'character' and 'had' is surface punctuation only: the definition ends at 'character'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mad Hatter is the eccentric tea-party host in Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland.

clue.text: Reflective article, if somewhat ingenuous

indicators.note: reflective says the article is seen as in a mirror, written back to front

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A thoughtful piece of writing that is a little naive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' suggests a thoughtful article, but it means mirrored, turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif is a variant of naive, describing someone artless and unsophisticated.

clue.text: A bomb angered constituents

indicators.note: constituents says the bomb is made up of the letters of angered, rearranged

explanation.surface: An explosive device annoyed the voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' rearranges ANGERED. The surface suggests voters in a constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small explosive weapon thrown by hand.

clue.text: Pilots giving orders

explanation.surface: Airline captains issuing commands.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct is to steer or guide, as a pilot does, and also to command or instruct.

clue.text: Stout that is maybe taken at the end of a meal

definitions.text: maybe taken at the end of a meal

parts.note: plump means stout or well-rounded
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dark beer that might be drunk after dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer, but it means fat, PLUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit pie is a typical pudding served as the last course.

clue.text: Written authority for a number to strike

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: A permit allowing a group of workers to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests authorising a strike; 'strike' means HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a short signed note, such as a voucher or permit.

clue.text: A fearsome beast can upset a girl a lot

indicators.note: upset says the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A frightening animal could greatly distress a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges A GIRL A LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: This large reptile with powerful jaws is a dangerous predator.

clue.text: Among the finest holiday resorts in Scotland

definitions.text: Among the finest holiday resorts in Scotland

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the run holiday resorts

explanation.surface: Praise for one of Scotland's best seaside towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' finds the town in 'holiday resorts'; the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a seaside town on the Firth of Clyde, long popular for holidays.

clue.text: Note it's the making of a small island

parts.note: A is a musical note
the word it, taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain feature makes an islet.
explanation.walkthrough: An ait, or eyot, is a river islet, especially on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: An ait is a small islet in a river.

clue.text: A diver needs dope

explanation.surface: Someone diving into water needs drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The loon is a diving water bird, and a loon is also a fool or idiot.

clue.text: The rate increase must be put off

parts.note: tempo is a rate or speed
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: A rise in interest rates has to be postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests delaying an interest-rate rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to delay or stall in order to gain time.

clue.text: None avail themselves of running water

parts.note: O is zero, none
to use is to avail oneself of

explanation.surface: Nobody takes advantage of a flowing stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is a river, a stream of moving water.

clue.text: One made rapid progress in the country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ran means moved quickly

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted ahead somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like the countryside, but it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia.

clue.text: Almost never rising before nightfall

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising says the letters read upwards
almost says the word never stops short of its final letter

explanation.surface: Something almost never goes up before dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts NEVER to NEVE, and 'rising' turns it upwards into EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Even is a poetic word for evening, the close of day.

clue.text: View taken about male wild-fowl

indicators.note: about says the word for view goes around the abbreviation for male

parts.note: to see is to view

explanation.surface: A man watches birds in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Smee is a dialect name for wild ducks, such as the smew or wigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A smee is a type of wild duck, a game bird.

clue.text: Restored control and reported

parts.note: a rein controls a horse, so to rein is to control
stated means reported or declared

explanation.surface: Someone regained control and announced it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinstated means put back in a former place or position.
